newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban government says four dissidents detained.
newsitem.headline: Cuban government says four dissidents detained.

text.p: The Cuban government said on Thursday that four dissidents were under arrest and were being investigated on suspicion of "counter-revolutionary" activities.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Miguel Alfonso confirmed the arrests in response to questions at a weekly foreign ministry briefing.
The four people detained early on Wednesday at their Havana homes are Vladimiro Roca, Martha Beatriz Roque, Felix Bonne and Rene Gomez Manzano.

The four run a group called the "Working Group of Internal Dissidence", that says it has the support of 14 other small dissident organisations in Cuba and is seeking to forge some unity among Cuba's small and fragmented opposition. The group has tried increasingly to draw attention to itself abroad in recent months.
Diplomatic and dissident sources had said earlier on Thursday that the four, leading dissidents who run a small opposition group on the Communist-ruled island, were in detention.

Alfonso gave no other details of what offences the four arrested people were supected of, except to confirm their names. However, he said Cuban law applied to all citizens, whether they were in favour of, or against, the revolution.
"There is no immunity for someone just because he declares himself a dissident," Alfonso said.

It is extremely unusual for the Cuban authorities to comment on arrests of dissidents or activities by Cuba's small and illegal dissident groups. President Fidel Castro's government calls the groups "grupusculos," tiny bodies with no significance, and says they are puppets of a U.S. policy seeking to destroy Cuba.
Diplomatic and dissidents sources said authorities also detained on Wednesday a dissident journalist called Luis Lopez Prendes. But Alfonso did not mention this case.
The reported detention of Lopez Prendes did not appear related to that of the Working Group members.
Alfonso's comments indicated none of the four Working Group members have yet been charged.

Roca's wife, Magaly de Armas, told reporters at the couple's home that state security officials arrived before dawn on Wednesday to take Roca away and then conducted an eight-hour search of the house, confiscating piles of possessions.

The confiscated material included 132 books, papers related to Roca's dissident work, a computer and computer printer, a typewriter, a video camera, a tape recorder, an English language course and dozens of pens and pencils, de Armas said.

Dissident sources said similar searches were carried out at the houses of Bonne and Gomez Manzano. Security officials confiscated a computer, three typewriters and numerous documents from Gomez Manzano's house, one dissident source said. They took two tape recorders and other office material from Bonne's house, the source added.
The Working Group has held two news conferences for foreign journalists since May, which is unusual.

At the most recent of these, last month, the group presented a paper sharply criticising a document prepared by the Communist Party for nationwide discussion ahead of the party's Congress this October.
"They are at the moment the highest-profile dissident group operating," said one western diplomatic source in Havana.

It did not appear the detentions of the four members of the Working Group were related to the bombing of two Havana hotels last Saturday. The Interior Ministry has said it has evidence the two small bombs, which slightly injured three people, were planted by people who came from the United States. The ministry has not given details of this evidence.
Roca, asked about the bombings at the weekend, was quick to strongly condemn them, saying he was against all terrorism.

But one dissident source said dissident journalist Lopez Prendes may have been detained because he made comments to the foreign media shortly after the bombs went off at the Nacional and Capri hotels in central Havana.

One dissident source said the round-up was possibly a preventative government measure ahead of an international leftist youth festival to be held in Havana July 28-Aug. 5, which more than 5,000 young people are expected to attend.
